Two things now catch it inside a verify run: the per-range bias is computed from maxFairFor, the one ceiling the draw reads, and must be exactly 0 for a rejection design (with maxFair = 2^32 the remainder is non-zero at 21 of the 25 ranges); and the branch is exercised on a deterministic vector (nonce 760455, cursor 12, range 13 must draw 6; with the branch gone it draws 1). Note what the 2^-32 bound alone would NOT catch: a plain chunk % range is biased by less than 2^-32 at every range 1..25, so the gate is the declared design's exact-zero, not the bound. This settles the AUDITOR'S draw. Whether the operator's server takes the branch remains ASSUMED (MANIFEST DL-3) — no client-side capture can witness it.
